:::{#def-squared-error-risk}
#### Squared-error risk

The **squared-error risk** of a prediction function $g(\Predvar)$
is the [risk](#def-risk) under squared error loss,
the expected square of its [prediction error](#def-prediction-error),
which compares $g(\Predvar)$ with the observed outcome $\Outvar$ of a new data point,
the estimand of the prediction:

$$\popriskf{g} \eqdef \E{\sqf{\prederr_g}}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-squared-error-risk}
#### Squared-error risk in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
the constant prediction $g_1(\Predvar) = 3$ has squared-error risk $\popriskf{g_1} = 5$.

:::
